title: Reconstruction of inert operadic algebras from their color diagrams
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], with cocartesian fibrations and inner fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad is an inner fibration $p:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ admitting cocartesian lifts of inert base arrows (opposites of consecutive-subinterval inclusions), satisfying $\mathcal M_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal M_{[1]}\times_{\mathcal M_{[0]}}\cdots\times_{\mathcal M_{[0]}}\mathcal M_{[1]}$; the zero-factor product is $\mathcal M_{[0]}$. It also satisfies this relative-limit axiom: if $I_n$ is the category of inert arrows $\alpha:[n]\to[i]$, $i=0,1$, and commuting inert triangles, and $C_\alpha$ are the cocartesian projections of $C\in\mathcal M_{[n]}$, then for every $X\in\mathcal M_{[m]}$ and $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ the canonical map $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(X,C)\to\lim_{\alpha\in I_n}\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha\phi}(X,C_\alpha)$ is an equivalence. The superscript denotes the homotopy fiber over the specified base arrow. An inert edge of $\mathcal M$ means a cocartesian edge over an inert base arrow. An algebra in a monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V$ is an inert-preserving functor $\mathcal M\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; write $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ for the full infinity category on these functors. Let $\mathcal M$ be such an operad with $\mathcal M_{[0]}$ a Kan complex and let $\mathcal V$ be any monoidal infinity category. Put $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}=\mathcal M\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$, regarded over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ by composition, and let $\tau:\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal M$ be the inclusion. Then $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, $\tau$ preserves inert edges, and $\tau_{[0]}$ is the identity. Restriction to the fiber over $[1]$ induces a natural equivalence
$$E:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},\mathcal V).$$
Its inverse sends $P$ and an object $x$ over $[n]$ to the tuple $(P(x_1),\ldots,P(x_n))$ under $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal V^n$, with the unique empty tuple when $n=0$; on inert structure it uses the corresponding projections. The equivalence is on infinity categories, including coherent transformations and all higher simplices. No colimit or presentability hypothesis on $\mathcal V$ is imposed.

external.place: Definition 3.4.1, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616

proof.text: Put $C=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$, $s:C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $B=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$. All fibers and all simplices over inert base diagrams are inherited from $\mathcal M$. The map $C\to B$ is an inner fibration by pullback. The composite $s$ is also inner: in a lifting problem over a simplex of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, an inner horn in $C$ contains all consecutive spine edges, so those base edges are inert. Their composites are inert too, and the whole prescribed base simplex lies in $B$; hence the original inner-fibration filler lies in $C$. Smallness is inherited. For fixed endpoints, the right-pinched mapping-space model has the same simplices as $\mathcal M$ over an inert arrow and none over a noninert arrow: its base simplices are degeneracies of that single arrow in the nerve of the ordinary base category.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Each original cocartesian lift $u:x\to y$ over an inert $\rho:[n]\to[m]$ stays $s$-cocartesian. Indeed, for $z$ over $[k]$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] over each discrete base arrow $\psi:[m]\to[k]$. If $\psi$ is inert, the two mapping fibers in its criterion are unchanged and the required equivalence is the original one. Otherwise both are empty: $\psi\rho$ is inert if and only if $\psi$ is inert, indeed, if $\rho^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=a+j$, then $(\psi\rho)^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=a+\psi^{\mathrm{op}}(j)$, so the successive increments are identical, also when $k=0$. This proves the mapping square for $s$. Conversely any $s$-cocartesian lift over $\rho$ has target equivalent, in the unchanged fiber, to the target of an original lift: both are initial in the lift category $L(x,\rho)$ formed in $C$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Its image in $\mathcal M$ is therefore cocartesian by the mapping criterion. Thus $\tau$ preserves inert edges, and $\tau_{[0]}$ is literally the identity. The Segal fiber-product axiom uses these same lifts and unchanged fibers, so is inherited. For the incidence axiom over an inert $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, all composites $\alpha\phi$ are inert and every mapping fiber and its coherence maps are unchanged; use the incidence axiom for $\mathcal M$. For noninert $\phi$ the left side is empty. Necessarily $n>0$, since every map to $[0]$ is inert. At least one $\rho_i\phi$ is noninert: if all restrictions of $\phi^{\mathrm{op}}$ to adjacent pairs had increment one, then $\phi^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=\phi^{\mathrm{op}}(0)+j$ would be a consecutive inclusion. The incidence diagram therefore has an empty color term, making its limit empty as well. This proves the relative-limit axiom, including $n=0$ where $I_0$ is the identity projection and no noninert case exists. Consequently $C$ is a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad with the same Kan zero-fiber.

proof.text: Write $C=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$, $A=\mathcal M_{[1]}$, $B=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$, and $s:C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. By steps 1–2, $C\to B$ is an inner fibration with cocartesian lifts of every base arrow. Apply [lem-coef-inert-color-coslice-components]: $A\subset C$ is full and $J_x=A\times_C C_{x/}$ is the disjoint union of $L(x,\rho_i)$, with the chosen inert projections $\alpha_i:x\to c_i$ initial. All categories are small, and at arity zero $J_x$ is empty. Thus [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] reduces local relative-limit lifting over $J_x$ to the discrete diagram on these projections, including the prescribed base cone and exact boundary.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Fix $h:A\to\mathcal V$. For $x\in C_{[n]}$, the selected boundary values in the preceding reduction are precisely $h(c_i)$, over the base projections $\rho_i$. By [lem-coef-inert-relative-tuple-cone] they have a $p$-limit cone over $[n]$ with exactly these targets and base edges. The existence clause of [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] extends this to a local $p$-limit on all of $J_x$, with the specified boundary $h$ after target projection and prescribed base cone $sl_x$. At $n=0$ the tuple lemma supplies the empty relative cone.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: The map $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an isofibration: it is inner by [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and every equivalence in the ordinary base is an identity and lifts by a degenerate edge. For the full inclusion $A\subset C$, the local lifts just constructed meet the right-hand hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence]. It gives an exact extension $H$ of $h$, over $s$, for which each $Hl_x$ is a $p$-limit. Thus every color diagram has a relative right Kan extension, with no further limits assumed.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Let $H:C\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ be a functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving inert edges. For every $x$, its cone on the chosen $\alpha_i$ has cocartesian edges. By [lem-coef-inert-relative-tuple-cone] this selected cone is a $p$-limit. The particular-cone clause of [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components], applied to the coslice decomposition above, makes $Hl_x$ a $p$-limit on all of $J_x$. Hence $H$ is relatively right Kan extended.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Conversely, let $H$ be relatively right Kan extended. The particular-cone clause of [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] makes its cone on the selected $\alpha_i$ a $p$-limit. By the converse in [lem-coef-inert-relative-tuple-cone], all $H(\alpha_i)$ are cocartesian. The same argument applies to every choice of inert color lifts, since each choice consists of initial objects in the coslice summands. In particular $H$ carries every inert edge to a color to a cocartesian edge.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: For any inert $a:x\to y$ over $\rho:[n]\to[m]$, choose inert color projections $b_j:y\to d_j$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], each composite $b_ja$ is cocartesian over the color projection $\rho_j\rho$, so the preceding step makes both $H(b_j)$ and $H(b_ja)$ cocartesian. Apply [lem-coef-operadic-inert-factor-equivalence] in $\mathcal V^\otimes$ to $u=H(a)$ over the inert $\rho$, the $p$-cocartesian projections $t_j=H(b_j)$, and the images under $H$ of the composition triangles, whose long edges $H(b_ja)$ are cocartesian. It follows that $H(a)$ is cocartesian. That lemma includes $m=0$, where every edge over the inert map to $[0]$ is cocartesian. Therefore the full subcategory of relative right Kan extensions is exactly $\operatorname{Alg}_C(\mathcal V)$, on all transformations and higher simplices.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: The existence result above verifies the hypothesis of [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-restriction]. Apply that theorem to $A\subset C$, $p$ and $s$. On the full subcategory just identified with the algebra category, actual restriction to $A$ is a trivial Kan fibration, hence an equivalence of infinity categories, including coherent transformations and all higher parameter simplices. Since the degree-one target fiber is $\mathcal V$, its target is $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal V)$. Naturality in $\mathcal M$ follows because restriction to colors commutes with operadic precomposition.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Let $E$ be restriction to $A=\mathcal M_{[1]}$. The previous step proves this actual restriction functor is an equivalence on infinity categories. For an extension of $P:A\to\mathcal V$, its inert projections at $x\in C_{[n]}$ are cocartesian, so the monoidal Segal equivalence in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] identifies its value with $(P(x_1),\ldots,P(x_n))$. For any inert $a:x\to y$ over $[n]\to[m]$, compose with each color projection of $y$; each resulting composite is an inert lift of the corresponding color projection of $x$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], its comparison with the chosen lift is an equivalence in the lift category, retaining the commuting triangle. Applying the extension functor retains that triangle and equivalence. Thus its image agrees, under the Segal identifications and these comparisons, with the projection to the indicated consecutive subtuple; this is an agreement up to coherent equivalence, not an equality of arbitrary chosen representatives. At $n=0$ the target fiber is equivalent to the point and this is the unique empty tuple, with contractible choices of representatives. Coherent quasi-inverses and their transformations exist by the restriction equivalence, rather than by choosing objectwise formulas without coherence. Naturality follows because restriction commutes with precomposition by operad maps and with inert-preserving monoidal postcomposition, including parameter simplices. No colimits or presentability entered: the only limits used were the relative tuple cones that are part of the monoidal axioms.
